stories.headline: Election Commission fixes website flaw exposing voter data after Reuters findings
stories.title: Election Commission fixes website flaw exposing voter data after Reuters findings
stories.summary: Researchers say flaw could have been easily ​abused
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A security flaw in India’s Election Commission (ECI) website that was allowing access to sensitive personal details and documents of some voters has been fixed, after Reuters discovered the vulnerability and alerted the institution.
Researchers said the flaw, which Reuters is the first to report, could have been easily abused.

The security issue, and the fix, come months ahead of elections in key Indian states, including the most populous, Uttar Pradesh, and while the ECI is facing growing public anger over a contentious drive to update voter lists.
Opposition parties and activists have said the drive has disenfranchised millions of voters to the benefit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party.
The ECI says it has complied with all regulations, while the BJP argues opposition groups are misleading the country after failing to win elections.

A Reuters review over more than a month of the ECI’s website showed that when a voter logged into their account and requested a telephone call with their local electoral officer, the network tab in an ordinary browser’s developer tools, opened with a simple right click, started showing the reference number of the form submitted online to enrol as voters or update their information.

On using those reference numbers to book the call, the same network details started revealing personal information such as the name, phone number, email, date of birth and address of the user, and even file paths to identification documents like passports that were submitted.

Such details were not otherwise visible on the browser’s main screen, which pointed to a vulnerability in the website’s code, said Indian security researchers Karan Saini and Ehraz Ahmed, who reviewed the Reuters findings step by step on the ECI website.
The bigger concern, researchers said, was the reference numbers followed a predictable pattern, meaning hackers could guess them, and automate downloads of large amounts of data.
A lay user is unlikely to follow such steps while requesting a call, but cybercriminals could, and also automate the steps to harvest data in bulk and abuse it, they said.
Reuters first shared its findings and sought comment from the ECI and its three commissioners on October 26, but they did not respond despite repeated requests.
On Thursday, an ECI spokesman said the commission’s information technology division had been asked to look into the findings.

stories.headline: Madras High Court refuses to reject election petition challenging CM Vijay’s victory from Perambur
stories.title: Madras High Court refuses to reject election petition challenging CM Vijay’s victory from Perambur
stories.summary: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan dismisses an application filed by the Chief Minister to reject the election petition filed by a voter, S. Dinesh
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Madras High Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) refused to reject an election petition filed against the victory of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay from the Perambur Assembly constituency, which he had retained after winning in two constituencies and resigning from the Tiruchi East seat.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan dismissed an application filed by the Chief Minister to reject the election petition filed by a voter, S. Dinesh, at the threshold, without forcing him to undergo the long-drawn process of facing a full-fledged trial to disprove the charges levelled against him by the election petitioner.

The judge said, the election petitioner had made out a cause of action for the conduct of a trial and that the veracity of the allegations levelled by him against the Chief Minister could be decided only after appreciating the evidence to be produced during the course of the trial.
What did the election plea say?
The election petition, filed through advocate V.R. Shanmuganathan, had accused the Chief Minister of having suppressed various facts related to his properties in the election affidavit.

The petitioner alleged that the Chief Minister had claimed ownership over 50 cents of government poromboke land at Vilpatti village in Kodaikanal, falsely declared a property sold by him for ₹35 crore at Padi in Chennai as his property worth ₹7 crore, and wrongly termed his Neelangarai bungalow as inherited property.

The petitioner had insisted that the election of the Chief Minister must be declared null and void for “wilful and deliberate” suppression, misrepresentation, and false declarations with respect to many of the immovable properties referred to in his 2026 election affidavit.
He said, Mr. Vijay had claimed to have purchased the Vilpatti agricultural land for a consideration of ₹30,000 in 1997 and that the present market value of the property was around ₹20 lakh.
However, an examination of the village ‘A’ register revealed that the property was actually a government poromboke land, the litigant said.
Similarly, the Chief Minister had declared to have purchased a non-agricultural land measuring 33,955 square feet at Porur in Chennai for a consideration of ₹9.13 crore in 2010.
However, an examination of Registration Department documents revealed that he had purchased only 20,773 sq.
for ₹7.5 crore.

stories.headline: U.S. 25% Tariff Threat: Why Is Washington Targeting India's PLI, Make In India & Atmanirbhar Bharat?
stories.title: U.S. 25% Tariff Threat: Why Is Washington Targeting India's PLI, Make In India & Atmanirbhar Bharat?
stories.summary: India wants to become a global manufacturing powerhouse. But the Trump administration is questioning the very policies designed to make that happen. In a major Section 301 investigation, the US Trade Representative has accused India's Make in India, Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Production Linked Incentive schemes of contributing to structural excess manufacturing capacity. Washington argues that government-backed production incentives, trade barriers and cheaper imports from non-market economies could distort global competition and hurt American businesses. It has proposed additional tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, with the rate potentially adjusted to 17% if India reaches a qualifying trade agreement with the US. New Delhi has rejected the excess-capacity allegation and wants trade concerns addressed through ongoing bilateral negotiations.

stories.title: Cabinet clears 50% increase in LS seats across states, ceiling to remain till 2051
reasons: source: event has 3 copies, primary source counted once

candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday approved a proposal to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha by 50% across states, with the revised ceiling to remain in place until 2051, sources told TOI.
The decision comes ahead of the special sitting of Parliament beginning November 30, during which the government is expected to take up changes to the delimitation-linked Women's Reservation Bill.

The proposed increase in Lok Sabha seats is understood to be part of the government's efforts to address concerns over the impact of delimitation on the representation of states, particularly those in southern India.
Earlier reports had indicated that the government was considering a formula to increase seats by 50% across states while retaining their existing inter-state share based on the 1971 Census.
The Cabinet meeting, chaired by PM Modi, was convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth, with all ministers asked to remain present, sources told ANI.
The government is considering amendments to the earlier legislation, which seeks to provide 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
The proposed changes follow the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha in April.
The earlier Bill linked the implementation of women's reservation to delimitation and proposed increasing the strength of the Lok Sabha from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850.
The special sitting of Parliament will begin with the Lok Sabha reconvening on November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will meet from December 2.
The sittings are expected to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.
Ayush Pandey is a journalist at The Times of India, covering breaking news, politics, defence, and major legal and policy developments across India and the world.
His reporting focuses on elections, national security, and institutional affairs, tracking the decisions and conflicts that shape public life.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today dismissed a plea seeking the removal of social media videos featuring an Italian politician allegedly questioning the country's democratic system during the Bharat Summit 2026 organized by the Telangana Government in Hyderabad on November 13-14.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Aparesh Singh dismissed the plea after briefly hearing Advocate Syed Rizwan Ahmad for the petitioner, who also sought regulation of speeches made by foreigners in events organised in India.
The matter was listed today after it was mentioned before the CJI last week.
During the mentioning, Ahmad described the remarks as a direct intervention in India's democratic affairs.
He said that the Italian delegate had not only raised the slogan but also translated it for other delegates attending the event.

"The participation of a foreign political representative in an Indian political campaign in this manner, including the raising of derogatory slogans and making prejudice political statements including the public endorsement of a particular political party and its leadership, raises a serious concern regarding the extent to which foreign political representatives may participate in or endorse the domestic political activities of an Indian political party violating the limits of International diplomacy, relations, ethics and corners of domestic political activities of India political parties while present within the territory of India, thereby raising questions concerning the permissible limits of international diplomacy and diplomatic relations."

stories.title: Supreme Court refuses urgent listing of plea against Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana
stories.summary: A Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant said anyone with a different view of the epic is free to make a film of their own, as the film is already running in theatres
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) declined to list for urgent hearing a petition challenging the release of the Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, saying anyone with a different view of the epic was free to make a film of their own.
A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana observed that the film was already running in theatres, and that those who wanted to watch it had already done so.
The petitioner’s counsel told the Court that the plea had been registered on November 23, 2026, and was yet to be listed for hearing.
“The movie has already been released.
Those who wanted to watch it have already seen it,” the CJI said.
When the counsel argued that “many facts have been distorted” in the film, Justice Bagchi said, “They made a movie as they understand, you make a movie as you understand.
Don’t waste the time of the court.
If you have a counter view about the epic, make a movie based on that.” As the lawyer pressed for an early hearing, the Bench said the matter would be listed in due course.
The petition alleges that the makers distorted mythological facts in their depiction of the epic.
Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, also referred to as Ramayana: Part 1, is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra.
It brings the epic to the big screen with Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana.
The ensemble cast includes Sunny Deol, Ravie Dubey, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court of India has directed the country's food regulator to introduce prominent red warning labels on packaged foods high in fat, sugar and salt, ruling that the fundamental rights to health, safe food and informed choice oblige the government to regulate unhealthy packaged foods.
The court gave the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) four months to review and finalise threshold levels for each “nutrient of concern”.

A bench comprising Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran on November 26, 2026 directed the food safety regulator to consider total sugars and saturated fat, rather than added sugar and added fat, alongside salt when determining these thresholds.

The court also directed that separate hexagonal warning labels carry standard pictorial representations of the nutrients of concern, accompanied by the words “HIGH FAT”, “HIGH SUGAR” or “HIGH SALT”, instead of a single combined hexagon.

The size of each warning label must be proportionate to the package's principal display panel, taking international practices into account, which ensures that each hexagon occupies not less than 4-5 per cent of that panel.

The 131-page judgment, delivered on a petition filed by the non-profit 3S and Our Health Society, interpreted Article 21 of the Constitution alongside Article 47, which makes improving nutrition, living standards and public health a primary duty of the state.
“Every meal is a quiet wager with one's own body, and a wager is fair only when the player can see the odds,” the bench observed.
“The issues before us turn on this simple fact – eating right is possible only when one knows what one is eating.
The label is the only witness at the point of sale.”
The judgment follows years of delays and changes in India's proposed front-of-pack nutrition labelling regulations.
In 2018, the Union government deferred a decision to introduce red warning labels on unhealthy packaged foods.
The FSSAI subsequently proposed a health star rating system, under which products would receive ratings based on their overall nutritional profile.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Appreciates Sucheta Dalal's PIL On Unclaimed Financial Assets, Disposes Plea Noting Measures Taken By Authorities
stories.title: Supreme Court Appreciates Sucheta Dalal's PIL On Unclaimed Financial Assets, Disposes Plea Noting Measures Taken By Authorities
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday disposed of a Public Interest Litigation filed by financial journalist Sucheta Dalal seeking directions to authorities to put in place measures enabling legal heirs to trace and claim unclaimed financial assets, including bank deposits, shares and mutual fund investments.

Noting that the Union Government, the Reserve Bank of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India have taken various administrative and regulatory steps to address the issue, the bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice R Mahadevan observed that judicial directions in that regard are not necessary.
At the same time, the bench placed on record its appreciation for Dalal for taking up a genuine public cause, saying that the case was an example of a responsible use of public interest litigation.
The bench also appreciated Advocate Prashant Bhushan for espousing the petitioners' cause with "passion and perseverance."

"The present proceedings were instituted not for securing any personal benefit but with the objective of protecting the financial interests of countless depositors, investors and their lawful claimants.
The petitioner has consistently drawn attention to the difficulties faced by ordinary citizens in identifying and recovering the unclaimed financial assets.
The concerns raised were genuine and the pursuit of the appropriate institutional measures to address them reflects a responsible exercise of public interest litigation," the bench observed.
However, the Court noted that the principal concerns raised have been substantially addressed by measures undertaken by the respondents (SEBI, RBI and the Department of Economic Affairs).

"We take on record the statements and assurances made in the respondents affidavits and expect the concerned authorities to continue the efforts towards improving the accessibility, efficiency, and transparency of the mechanism for identifying and recovering unclaimed financial assets.
No useful purpose will be served by keeping the petition pending for further monitoring of the regulatory measures already undertaken.
Any specific grievances concerning unclaimed financial assets may be pursued before the competent authority in accordance with law," the bench added.
The bench had reserved judgment on November 17.

stories.headline: India-US trade pact and tariffs: An explainer
stories.title: India-US trade pact and tariffs: An explainer
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 27: India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of their bilateral trade agreement (BTA) in February this year, following negotiations that were launched in February 2025. But changes in Washington's tariff structure have brought the two sides back to the negotiating table. The US has proposed a fresh set of tariffs on 14 economies, including India. Here is an explainer to understand the developments so far. Why this trade pact? India is pursuing the agreement to safeguard the competitiveness of its exports amid high American tariffs and secure an edge over rival South and South East Asian manufacturing economies. Why these tariffs? The US is using tariffs against its trading partners such as India to address trade deficits, shield domestic industries from foreign competition and press countries to negotiate trade agreements on terms favourable to Washington. The US has alleged that trading partners like India and China impose steep import duties and restrictive regulations on American goods while enjoying low-tariff access to the US market. What is a tariff? It is a customs or import duty imposed by the importing country on goods entering its territory and paid by the importer. Tariffs increase the cost of imported goods and can make them more expensive than domestically produced products. They are used to protect domestic industries, generate government revenue and influence trade flows. Why US market important for India? The US has been India's largest trading partner since 2021-22. Exports grew 0.92 pc to USD 87.3 billion during 2025-26, while imports increased 15.95 per cent to USD 52.9 billion. India's trade surplus with the US declined to USD 34.4 billion in 2025-26 from USD 40.89 billion in 2024-25. The US is India's largest export destination for sectors such as textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, gems and jewellery, chemicals and electronics. Any increase in tariffs could affect the price competitiveness of Indian products and exporters' ability to retain or expand their market share. Why tariff landscape in US changing? The US announced a 25 pc duty from August 7, 2025. An additional 25 pc tariff was imposed on Indian goods as a penalty for New Delhi's continued purchase of Russian oil. After this order, the total tariff on Indian goods, barring an exemption list, rose to 50 pc. On February 2, 2026, India and the US agreed on a trade deal, under which Washington agreed to bring down the reciprocal tariff on Indian goods to 18 pc. On February 20, the US Supreme Court struck down the reciprocal tariff system. The Donald Trump administration subsequently turned to Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the US to impose tariffs following investigations into alleged unfair trade practices. The probes into forced labour and excess manufacturing capacity are part of Washington's efforts to rebuild its tariff regime under an alternative legal provision. On July 24, the US imposed a 10 and 12.5 pc tariff on 60 countries, including India (10 pc), under Section 301, citing concerns related to 'forced labour'. What triggered the latest development? The US Trade Representative (USTR) on November 25 announced the findings of its second Sec 301 investigations into structural excess manufacturing capacity in 14 economies, including India, and proposed additional tariffs on their goods. For India, it proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent, while indicating that the rate could be adjusted to 17 per cent if the two countries reach a trade agreement. US allegations on India? The USTR has alleged that India's industrial policies (such as the 'Make in India' initiative and PLI schemes), manufacturing expansion plans, labour protections, financial practices and market access barriers contribute to structural excess capacity and hurt American firms. The report has identified sectors such as steel, solar, pharmaceuticals, medical devices and information and communications technology as areas of concern. India's response? India has rejected the allegations, stating that it does not have structural excess capacity in any sector. It emphasised that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of the trade pact negotiations. It said India remains committed to working closely with the US towards the early conclusion of the India-US BTA in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026. Joint statement? The two countries announced that they have reached a framework for an interim agreement regarding reciprocal and mutually beneficial trade. The terms of that pact include: - India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on all US industrial goods and a wide range of food and agri products. - The US will apply a reciprocal tariff rate of 18 pc on Indian goods, subject to the successful conclusion of the interim agreement. - Both will address non-tariff barriers that affect bilateral trade. Important: "In the event of any changes to the agreed-upon tariffs of either country, the US and India agree that the other country may modify its commitments." - India intends to purchase USD 500 billion of US energy products, aircraft and aircraft parts, precious metals, technology products, and coking coal over the next 5 years. \ Current status of talks? India has stated on multiple occasions that the deal has been finalised and will be signed once the US tariff framework is in place and India gets a comparative advantage over its competitor nations. Comparative advantage means securing lower US import tariffs and better market access than rival manufacturing countries, such as Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, and China, so Indian exporters can price goods more competitively in the US market. Has India received the advantage ? The latest USTR's report has proposed a 17 per cent tariff on India if the trade pact is finalised. It gives only one per cent edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18 per cent deal rate) and a 3 per cent edge over Vietnam and China (20 per cent deal rate). Without a pact, tariffs against India could go up to 25 pc. However, according to experts, Indian exporters could face a tariff disadvantage against goods from several other countries in the US market, as Washington's latest Section 301 investigation into structural excess capacity covers only 14 trading partners, while the probe into forced-labour-related trade practices covers 60 countries. This leaves a much larger group of economies (including Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the Philippines and Turkiye) potentially outside the additional tariff action, giving their exporters a relative cost advantage in the US market. Experts view While exporters are urging the government to finalise the pact at the earliest, think tank GTRI said that with the threat of up to 100 pc Graham tariffs still looming, New Delhi must reject a one-sided trade deal and defend its industrial expansion sector by sector as serving legitimate domestic, export, and future demand. What next The USTR has decided to schedule public hearings on its proposals on January 25 and has sought written comments from interested persons by January 5 as part of the final regulatory requirements before the tariffs come into effect.

The US Trade Representative (USTR) on November 25 announced the findings of its second Sec 301 investigations into structural excess manufacturing capacity in 14 economies, including India, and proposed additional tariffs on their goods.
For India, it proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent, while indicating that the rate could be adjusted to 17 per cent if the two countries reach a trade agreement.

The USTR has alleged that India's industrial policies (such as the 'Make in India' initiative and PLI schemes), manufacturing expansion plans, labour protections, financial practices and market access barriers contribute to structural excess capacity and hurt American firms.

It emphasised that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of the trade pact negotiations.
It said India remains committed to working closely with the US towards the early conclusion of the India-US BTA in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026.
Joint statement?
The two countries announced that they have reached a framework for an interim agreement regarding reciprocal and mutually beneficial trade.
The terms of that pact include: - India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on all US industrial goods and a wide range of food and agri products.
- The US will apply a reciprocal tariff rate of 18 pc on Indian goods, subject to the successful conclusion of the interim agreement.
- Both will address non-tariff barriers that affect bilateral trade.

\ Current status of talks?
India has stated on multiple occasions that the deal has been finalised and will be signed once the US tariff framework is in place and India gets a comparative advantage over its competitor nations.

Comparative advantage means securing lower US import tariffs and better market access than rival manufacturing countries, such as Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, and China, so Indian exporters can price goods more competitively in the US market.
Has India received the advantage?
The latest USTR's report has proposed a 17 per cent tariff on India if the trade pact is finalised.
It gives only one per cent edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18 per cent deal rate) and a 3 per cent edge over Vietnam and China (20 per cent deal rate).
Without a pact, tariffs against India could go up to 25 pc.

However, according to experts, Indian exporters could face a tariff disadvantage against goods from several other countries in the US market, as Washington's latest Section 301 investigation into structural excess capacity covers only 14 trading partners, while the probe into forced-labour-related trade practices covers 60 countries.

This leaves a much larger group of economies (including Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the Philippines and Turkiye) potentially outside the additional tariff action, giving their exporters a relative cost advantage in the US market.

While exporters are urging the government to finalise the pact at the earliest, think tank GTRI said that with the threat of up to 100 pc Graham tariffs still looming, New Delhi must reject a one-sided trade deal and defend its industrial expansion sector by sector as serving legitimate domestic, export, and future demand.

The USTR has decided to schedule public hearings on its proposals on January 25 and has sought written comments from interested persons by January 5 as part of the final regulatory requirements before the tariffs come into effect.
